interest: This document file sheet is useful for social, legal, and labor historians of interwar Japan as it pinpoints the implementation date (October 6, 1933) of key Japanese child welfare legislation protecting minors from abuse and economic exploitation as wage-earners. It demonstrates the U.S. State Department's active monitoring of domestic social reforms and child labor regulations in imperial Japan during the early Showa period. Additionally, it provides an essential archival cross-reference bridging the State Department's mother and child welfare classification (894.4055) with its general labor and wage-earner files (894.5047).
overview: This file consists of a single State Department document file cross-reference sheet (894.4055/1) directing researchers to Despatch No. 702, filed under decimal number 894.5047/2. The despatch, sent from Tokyo by Arthur Garrels on October 6, 1933, reports on the new Child Welfare Law that came into force in Japan on that date to protect children from persecution and exploitation as wage-earners, summarizing the salient features of the legislation.

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet referring to Tokyo Despatch No. 702 on the enactment and key features of Japan's Child Welfare Law.
subfiles.summary: This document file sheet records that Despatch No. 702, dated October 6, 1933, from Arthur Garrels in Tokyo, was placed in file 894.5047/2. The despatch details a new Child Welfare Law that went into effect in Japan on October 6, 1933, designed to protect children from persecution and various forms of wage-earning exploitation. It notes that the despatch provides the salient features of the new statute.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Tokyo Despatch No. 702 on Child Welfare Law
